observation.pivot_math: computed assuming a simple point at (1.2,0,0.7) rotating around pivot (1.2,0,0) would land exactly at (1.2,0,-0.7) after 180deg

reason: spin the upper attachment face 180deg around pivot (1.2,0,0), axis Y, to sweep the handle tube -- intended to land precisely on the pre-cut lower hole

result_state.note: REAL MISCALCULATION FOUND AFTER THE FACT: the starting face spans a range of Y (it is not on the pivot's meridian plane, its 4 corners have differing Y values), so treating it as a single point at (1.2,0,0.7) was wrong -- corners did not land back on the cylinder surface (final radius 1.37 vs intended 1.2), offset from the hole by roughly 0.18 units. Not silently ignored -- diagnosed via direct vertex inspection, and the fix (bridge_edge_loops, which does not require exact alignment) is the next decision.
